messages:
michael: Heads-up — after the traffic spike yesterday the continuous-batcher fell into a long tail where small tenants starved and large requests pushed the coalescer to max window. I want to capture the follow-ups: deferred reservation idea + an aging watermark to reduce starvation. Thoughts?

dana: Can you sketch the deferred reservation idea? is it like lease + delayed allocation?

michael: Yep. Idea: when admission accepts a request we allocate a soft reservation token instead of immediate slab space. Token holds reservation for T_reserve ms. If the slot fills (batch formed) we convert token->slot; otherwise token expires and score decays. This lets us keep small requests in the admission queue without forcing large batches to wait.

ryan: Sounds like soft tickets. How do we prevent token hoarding by noisy tenants?

michael: Two levers: per-tenant concurrent token caps + token-cost accounting. Each token carries a small credit charge that increments a tenant's debt ledger; high debt reduces future token success probability. Also token lifetime is tunable per-PQ class.

lee: Neat. Where does the aging watermark come in?

michael: Aging watermark is a moving threshold used by the coalescer to prioritize older tokens. Normally coalescer sorts by estimated latency impact and seq length; we add an age multiplier that boosts priority for tokens older than W ms. That avoids perpetual deferral for latency-sensitive small requests.

sam: Any changes needed to KV cache affinity? token->slot conversion should try to pick a batch with matching KV signature to avoid warmup miss.

michael: Exactly. Token metadata must include a small KV fingerprint (e.g., first N token ids or hashed prefix). During conversion we prefer batches with matching fingerprint. If none, we fall back but mark a warmup hint for prefetch.

ryan: Implementation risk: this increases per-request metadata and memory churn. Also matching is O(batches) which could be heavy.

michael: Implementation sketch: tokens are small structs (tenant, age, kv_hint, token_id) kept in ring buffer. Matching uses bucketed fingerprint indices (hash -> candidate batch queue) so average O(1) lookup. We'll add a GC pass every few seconds to clear expired tokens.

lee: Can we see config example for token lifetime & debt?

michael: Sure: ```json
{
  "token_lifetime_ms": 50,
  "token_cost": 0.02,
  "tenant_token_cap": 10,
  "debt_decay_ms": 60000
}
```

sam: How do we evaluate? what metrics are most relevant?

michael: Minimal experiment plan: 1) Canary with 10% of machines; 2) SLOs: p50/p95 latency for small (<64 token) vs large (>512 token) requests, cold-kv miss rate, global throughput, and token conversion success ratio. Also check KV cache eviction churn.

infra-bot: deploy request queued: PR 5123 (deferred-reservations) -> staging, canary=10% -> owner=michael

ryan: One more tradeoff: this shifts complexity into admission/coalescer boundary. Maybe instead of tokens we could extend the enqueue shape to include a soft deadline hint and let existing windowing use that?

michael: Yeah that's the alternative — soft deadline hints are simpler but don't give us explicit accounting for token debt/caps. Tokens let us throttle noisy tenants proactively. I think we should prototype token approach but keep soft-deadline fallback.

lee: Would love to see a small perf sim before rolling to canary. Can we run the sim with synthetic tenant mixes (1 hot large tenant + many small interactive)?

michael: On it. I'll wire up a sim with the existing batcher-sim harness and add token model knobs. Expect results by EOD tomorrow.

sam: +1 on sim. Also add telemetry: token_issued, token_expired, token_converted, token_rejected_by_debt, kv_match_on_convert (bool), prefetch_hint_sent.

michael: Good checklist. If sim looks sane we'll open the staging PR and add canary telemetry dashboards. Thanks all :thumbsup:
